transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-25
- Time: 09:00 AM PT
- Duration: 45 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (CTO, Aurum), Sana Iqbal (Head of Security, Aurum), Rafael Gomez (Platform Eng, Aurum)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
Aurum Tech is evaluating Redwood for inference serving across Hosted and Dedicated modes with a potential Private deployment later. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO attestations, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logging granularity, KMS/HSM key management (bring-your-own-key), encryption at rest/in-transit, and data retention/ERASING policies. Customer requested attestation docs and a technical deep-dive/POC for dedicated capacity focusing on KMS integration and audit logs.

Topics covered:
- Compliance posture (SOC 2, ISO27001)
- Identity: SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC mapping to customer AD
- Audit logs: retention, access, exportability, tamper-resistance
- Encryption/KMS: BYOK, HSM options, key rotation, access controls
- Data residency and retention/deletion policies (PII handling)
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency, cost, isolation)
- Next steps and POC plan

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side — I'm Maya, AE here at Redwood, with Liam and Priya from our solutions team.
[00:08] Daniel Park: Thanks. I'm Daniel — CTO at Aurum. We've got Sana on security and Rafael who runs platform. We'll try to keep this focused on security posture and what it would take to run production workloads.
[00:16] Sana Iqbal: Hi all. We want to understand your SOC2 status, ISO, and then the SSO and key management. We have stricter controls for customer data.
[00:23] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely, thanks Sana. Quick high-level: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and we also have ISO27001 attestation — I can share the certs after this call. For an enterprise flow we support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning, and RBAC that maps to group claims.
[00:38] Sana Iqbal: When you say RBAC maps to group claims, can we enforce least-privilege per environment? We need separate roles for dev/test/prod and strict audit on who can run models and access logs.
[00:50] Priya Nair: Yep, you can map SAML groups to Redwood roles. For Dedicated/Private environments you can get tenant-level isolation and admin-only controls. We also support route-level permissions in the Console so you can restrict model deploys and invocation.
[01:06] Rafael Gomez: Can you explain the difference between Hosted and Dedicated from a data isolation and log perspective? If we use Hosted, our logs and telemetry sit in Redwood's control plane, right? How long are those retained, and can we export them?
[01:21] Liam O'Connor: Good question. Hosted keeps control plane and operational logs in our managed system — we retain standard logs for 90 days by default but you can configure longer retention as an add-on. All audit logs can be exported via S3 export or streamed to a customer's SIEM. For Dedicated, you get a separate tenant and we can also enable log forwarding to your S3 or Splunk — same for Private, where you manage the environment.
[01:41] Sana Iqbal: Is audit log tamper-resistance supported? We need immutable logs for certain workflows.
[01:46] Priya Nair: We provide append-only audit logs in the control plane and we sign logs for integrity. For the highest level of assurance we recommend forwarding logs to your own storage (S3 with write-once policies or your SIEM) in Dedicated or Private so you control retention and immutability.
[02:01] Daniel Park: KMS, BYOK — how mature is your BYOK flow? Do we have to rotate keys through Redwood, or can we control key lifecycle entirely from our KMS/HSM?
[02:12] Liam O'Connor: We support Bring-Your-Own-Key via cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM-backed keys for Dedicated/Private options. You can perform key rotation from your KMS and Redwood will request short-lived wrapping keys. For Hosted we offer a managed KMS with customer-managed keys option — but for strict requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private so keys never leave your KMS.
[02:36] Sana Iqbal: So in Hosted if we choose CMK, are keys in our account or in Redwood's account? We want keys in our account with limited Redwood access.
[02:45] Liam O'Connor: For Hosted CMK, we can do cross-account key policies where the key lives in your AWS account and Redwood uses a limited role to encrypt/decrypt. It's more common in Dedicated/Private that the keys are fully under the customer's control. We'll include a diagram in the follow-up.
[02:59] Rafael Gomez: Network — for Private do you support VPC peering or private link? We need to avoid public egress for inference traffic.
[03:08] Priya Nair: We support both VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink depending on the cloud provider. For Private deployments you can run the control plane in your VPC or use a private control plane option. We'll share specifics for peering, route tables, and port lists.
[03:22] Sana Iqbal: Data retention — if a customer requests deletion of PII from logs and cached prompts, what does your flow look like? Is there an audit trail for deletion requests?
[03:33] Maya Chen: We have a data lifecycle policy. For Hosted, we support per-customer retention settings and deletion APIs; we log deletion requests and provide confirmation receipts. For Dedicated and Private, you can set retention on your side and we can support an API to purge KV caches and request logs. We'll document the SLA for deletion during POC scoping.
[03:52] Daniel Park: About KV cache and prefixes — we use some prompt caching on our side. Do you persist KV caches on disk? What's the encryption and retention there?
[04:01] Liam O'Connor: KV caches are stored on instance-local storage for performance and are encrypted at rest. For Dedicated/Private you can enforce that the storage is encrypted with your keys. They get rotated/evicted per configured TTL and can be purged on demand.
[04:15] Sana Iqbal: What about compliance artifacts — pen test reports, third-party audits, bug bounty?
[04:21] Priya Nair: We have a red team assessment summary and we can share an executive summary; we do run regular pen tests with third-party firms and have a bug bounty program. Full reports are under NDA but the attestation and remediation summaries we'll share.
[04:35] Rafael Gomez: Are there export controls or data residency constraints we should be aware of? Our EU customers require EU-only processing for certain datasets.
[04:43] Liam O'Connor: We support regional hosting; for EU-only workloads we can pin inference to EU regions and for Private you can run on-prem or in your cloud regions. We'll note region pins in the follow-up.
[04:55] Daniel Park: One of our concerns is endpoint egress when using model fallbacks. If you fallback to a smaller model hosted elsewhere, how are data flows handled?
[05:05] Maya Chen: Good point — fallback policies only route to approved model variants in allowed regions. For enterprise configs, you can lock down allowed fallbacks to the same region or tenant. We'll show how routing policies are enforced.
[05:18] Sana Iqbal: For SSO/SAML and SCIM, what's the provisioning latency? We don't want a long delay when revoking access.
[05:25] Priya Nair: SCIM provisioning is near-real-time for user creation and deactivation; group syncs happen on a configurable cadence but short intervals are recommended. We also offer a connector for immediate deprovision via SCIM delta syncs.
[05:38] Rafael Gomez: Auditing access to stored prompts/embeddings — can we get field-level access logs, like who retrieved a specific embedding or invoked a particular model route?
[05:48] Liam O'Connor: We capture per-request metadata including requester identity, model and route, tokens used, and outcome. For high-compliance customers we can provide enhanced logging with object-level access events exported to your SIEM.
[06:00] Daniel Park: Encryption in transit — mTLS?
[06:03] Priya Nair: Yes, we support TLS 1.2/1.3 and mutual TLS for Private deployments. For Hosted we rely on TLS with certificate pinning and IP allowlists; Dedicated/Private can use mTLS for stronger guarantees.
[06:16] Maya Chen: Quick recap on the ask: Aurum wants SOC2/ISO docs, diagrams for BYOK and VPC peering, and a POC focused on KMS integration and audit log export. We'll set a technical deep-dive with your platform team next week.
[06:29] Sana Iqbal: That sounds right. Also want a sample of the audit log schema and retention options in writing.
[06:36] Liam O'Connor: We'll attach an example audit log schema and sample entries.
[06:40] Rafael Gomez: Anything else on encryption key lifecycle? How do you handle key compromise or rotation notifications?
[06:47] Liam O'Connor: If a key is rotated or revoked, Redwood treats those as configuration changes — for BYOK we rely on your KMS and we surface webhook events. We can also support an incident playbook integration where we notify a security contact and provide a verification path.
[07:02] Daniel Park: SLA and support channels — does Dedicated include an SLA for latency?
[07:07] Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated comes with uptime and P90 latency targets per contract. We'll include sample SLAs in the follow-up.
[07:14] Maya Chen: Great. Any final questions?
[07:16] Sana Iqbal: One quick one — can we do offline key escrow for long-term archival encryption? Some of our legal workflows require keys that can be escrowed.
[07:25] Liam O'Connor: We can discuss escrow options; typically that becomes part of a Private/on-prem arrangement or a dedicated KMS workflow. We'll flag that for legal in the next steps.
[07:34] Daniel Park: OK thanks, that's helpful. Next steps then: send docs, schedule deep technical POC, Rafael will share VPC/network info.
[07:42] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items and propose time slots for the POC deep dive.

End of transcript.
